primary_outcome: the JSON incident report /app/triage.py writes for an evidence directory equals the report case-guide.md gives (initial access, sources, accounts, privilege escalation, persistence, first and last activity)

authority.anchor: may have run behind by a fixed amount

obligations.wrong_but_plausible: collection year for every line; ignore the step or apply it to auth.log only; local time as UTC; always add the correction

obligations.contribution: hostile = five btmp failures within 600 s; initial access = earliest wtmp login from a hostile address

authority.anchor: The team calls an address hostile

separability.rationale: the initial login seeds the attacker address/account fixed point and first activity

obligations.wrong_but_plausible: first successful login; any address with five failures; strict <600; counting auth.log failures

obligations.contribution: attacker keys (fingerprints of keys in attacker accounts' histories), attacker logins/addresses/accounts to a fixed point

obligations.wrong_but_plausible: ignore key logins from other addresses; take keys from every history

obligations.contribution: first sudo to root on a TTY whose open session is an attacker session (or an attacker root login)

obligations.contribution: earliest and latest attacker event over failures, logins, logouts, sudo, persistence ctimes and in-session stamped history

universal_rule.anchor: Every rule in the guide holds for every such directory

silence.anchor: Every evidence directory records exactly one intrusion by one

coverage_envelope.anchor: The other hosts differ in everything the guide lets vary

seeds: solution/seal.py SEED_BASE 5000000, sealed; verifier draws nothing
determinism.order_sensitivity: list fields compared as sets; tests pinned by name

unclaimed_units_rationale.test_outputs.py::test_candidate_cannot_r: harness isolation check (protected ground truth), not a report rule

removed_obligations.reason: rescope E2 (clearance CRS-C Minor): a host clock that ran ahead and was set back makes host times overlap; month-end steps, collector-settled logins in the overlap and rotation interactions multiplied reference obligations without adding to the causal core, so rule 1 is narrowed to a clock that ran behind and was set forward

former_anchor.anchor: may have been wrong by a fixed amount

exact_output_requirements.rationale: the report is consumed by the team's case tooling; keys and the UTC time format are fixed

authority_anchor.anchor: writes one JSON object with exactly these keys

documented_exceptions.reason: from-scratch analyzer, not a repair: no shipped behaviour to keep. contract-closure §1: a from-scratch task declares the domain it grades and grades nothing outside it; the anchor is that domain declaration and named_cases is empty.

record parsing and JSON serialization are written by the solver (no supplied package), so no support row can be implementation_complete; folded into the core obligations whose evidence they read; formats fully specified in record-formats.md.

graded evidence sets (auth logs, binary wtmp/btmp, listings) are ~315 KB; they are sealed as tests/evidence/<family>.tar.gz (binary, outside the panel text budget) while every expected report and each case's range facts stay plain JSONL under tests/expected; ROSTER pins both.

from-scratch analyzer: no solution/fix.patch; wrong paths are whole-deliverable patches of environment/app/triage.py (stub -> wrong analyzer) scored by reports/.../tools/score.sh, the same separate verifier image the harness uses.

'Use only the Python standard library' and 'must not depend on anything in /app/evidence' are enforced by the harness itself rather than by a test that could fail: every run is python3 -I -S (no site-packages) in a verifier image whose /app holds only triage.py and docs (no /app/evidence). A submission breaking either cannot produce a report there, so it fails every family test.
